scope: Proposition 3.4 (Root eigenline and deepest residue) of the manuscript “B-semiampleness for compact log-smooth Kähler fibrations” (preprints/B-semiampleness-for-compact-log-smooth-Kahler-fibrations-September-10-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 afad4b593eede2dd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let k be the maximal number of horizontal coefficient-one components meeting in a good fiber, constant after shrinking U. For the local root family above: (i) Fd Vχ = OV ◦ τ. This line lies in the single pure weight grade GrW d+k Vχ. (ii) Choose a depth-k intersection component downstairs dominating the good open. After a good-open base change selecting one connected component A∗ x of its fibers, take every root-cover sheet above that component. Iterated residue identifies the line in (i), through its pure grade and with the Tate twist removed, with the highest eigenline of the resolved root cover of the induced klt volume on A∗ x. In degree m this is the specified plurivolume identification from SNC adjunction. (iii) These highest-line identifications preserve generators in canonical extensions on unipo- tent disks. In a disk model satisfying the hypotheses of (3.2), its extended mixed top line projects isomorphically to the same pure line. If k = 0, the intersection is the whole original fiber, there is no removed divisor, and the pure root-cover cohomology itself provides the line.
